{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
seeker: Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
seeker: Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
supporter: That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
seeker: It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
seeker: Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
supporter: That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
seeker: I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
supporter: That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
seeker: A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
supporter: It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
seeker: You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.
supporter: That's a positive perspective. How do you plan to keep your connections going from here?
seeker: I'm thinking of arranging a small family gathering, something more joy-filled, to keep everyone in touch.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea! It could be a new tradition that brings everyone closer.
seeker: I hope so. It feels good just talking about it. Thanks for listening and helping me work through this.
supporter: Anytime, Amanda. Remember, you're taking meaningful steps. Keep nurturing those connections.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello, how are you ?
supporter: Hello
supporter: I am good, how are you?
seeker: I'm doing well, but it could have been better
supporter: What seems to be bothering you tonight?
seeker: Yes, my boy friend of 3 years has refused to take our relationship to the next level and I'm kind of getting tired, I don't want to play games anymore
supporter: So just to make sure I understand completely, you are ready to move on to the next step of your relationship and you don't feel as though your boyfriend is and this is making you anxious and upset, 
seeker: exactly, I hate to feel that I'm wasting my time
supporter: I completely understand that, as I was in a long term relationship and I felt as though my girlfriend at the time did not want to take things to the next step and I was not happy about it. 
seeker: Yes, I love him so dearly to want to settle down with him, but if he doesn't want that for me I would rather call it quits now than continue and be disappointed at the long run. 
supporter: Have you had that conversation with him? I know it might be a difficult conversation to have, but it is often good to get expectations out in the open so you are on the same page with your partner. 
seeker: Yes, sort of and he gave me the impression that he is not there yet and that was a like almost a year ago, I don't want it to look like I'm pushing him if I try to talk to him again about it. His nonchalant attitude in not seeing the seriousness of it is killing me, I'm just not happy. 
supporter: That is tough, but sometimes people just portray things differently, for instance I am also very laid back and nonchalant about most things which can lead to miscommunications. 
supporter: I don't think it would be pushing if you haven't had that conversation in almost a year.
seeker: I hope you are right, just don't want to come across as a desperate person and that's why I'm setting myself up to call it quits if he tries to sound like he sounded the last time. 
supporter: You need to know where he is so you can make a good decision for yourself!
supporter: I know it is difficult, but I know you can get through it!
seeker: You are right, that's exactly what I'm going to do because the wait is killing me. 
supporter: Good, I am happy for you!
seeker: Thank you very much, you've been a great help
supporter: I am glad I was able to help!
seeker: Thanks, it was nice chatting with you.
supporter: You're welcome! If you need any more help just chat back with us again.
seeker: no problem, take care.
supporter: You as well!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: I feel sad, and feel like need help
supporter: Can you identify why you feel sad?
seeker: yes, my aunt pass away a couple weeks ago
seeker: and since then im feeling really sad
supporter: It is natural to feel sad when someone you care about dies.
seeker: IS there something I can do to feel better?
supporter: Are you with family?   Sometimes it helps to be with others who are grieving?
seeker: No, I live alone, my family lives in another state
supporter: Being by yourself is rough after a death.    Can you talk with your family by phone?   Do you have a friend who has gone through a similar loss?
seeker: I feel like everybody is in their own bussines and have no time to hear my complains
seeker: I talk to my family, but the whole family is not doing really fine
supporter: It sounds like you feel people think you are complaining when you talk about your Aunt's death making you sad.    Is that correct?
seeker: yes
supporter: Do you feel you are complaining?
seeker: yes, I feel like noone wants to listen
seeker: I need to do something by mnyself
seeker: Can you recommend someting for me to do to feel better?
supporter: My own experiences with family deaths is they are sad.    I just wanted to "feel better".    My experience was it did not help to complain about "being sad" but it did help to talk about why I missed my family member.     If no one was available,   sometimes I would journal.   Do you think that might help you?
seeker: Well maybe it could works, to mantain distracted
seeker: thank you
supporter: You are welcome.    I am sorry about your Aunt.
seeker: Thnak you, I think it helps to have someone to chat
seeker: Makes me feel better to chat a bit with you, helped me to relax
supporter: That is why I am here.     Is there anything else you would like to chat about?
seeker: I hink, Im fine for now. I will try to keep myself focus on different things
seeker: and try to chat a bit more at leaat with my family
supporter: Good bye?
seeker: Good bye!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-20","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: hi there
supporter: Hello! How are you doing? 
seeker: I'm not doing so good at the moment. I'm feeling very stressed and burned out from work
supporter: That sounds very frustrating. Is this a recent development at your job? 
seeker: It's been building up for a while now, but it's really starting to get a but overwhelming
supporter: I can understand how that can have an effect on your mental well-being. Have you spoken to your supervisor about your frustrations at work? 
seeker: I have, but sometimes I feel like she doesn't really listen and she sort of talks over me a lot
supporter: It sounds like you don't feel listened to. 
seeker: That's right... I guess that is quite a lot of the problem. 
seeker: I don't mind so much the work, I know it is busy for everyone right now, it's a combination of the workload plus not being listened to
supporter: I had a similar issue at my last job. My supervisor constantly spoke over me in meetings, and it would drive me crazy. I never could get a word in edge-wise. 
seeker: Yeah, that sounds a lot like what I am experiencing
supporter: Are you considering switching jobs? 
seeker: It's been in the back of my mind, but it's a hard time just now with everything else going on
supporter: Absolutely. It's a rough time job searching under the best of circumstances. 
seeker: It is. 
supporter: Have you tried reaching out to anyone in your network to look for a new position? It helped me when I was previously job searching. 
seeker: I haven't, but it might be worth getting in touch with some people
supporter: Absolutely. I also spoke with a therapist before and it helped me a lot. 
supporter: Have you considered reaching out to a professional to talk to? 
seeker: I did consider that, but aren't they expensive?
supporter: They can be, but many local governments and municipalities have therapists that work on a sliding scale if the financial aspect of therapy is a concern. 
supporter: Therapy can definitely be a large expense though. 
seeker: It might be worth it in the long run though I guess, if it helps how I am feeling
supporter: If it helps to reframe the expense, you can try to think of it as an investment in your mental health. 
seeker: Yes, that sounds like a more positive way of thinking of it
supporter: The therapist could likely give you some tools to help manage the frustrations at your workplace more constructively. 
seeker: Yes, I imagine they will have come across this before so will be able to help
supporter: Absolutely. I hope that you're able to find some peace at your workplace with your boss. 
seeker: Thank you, you have helped a lot
seeker: Helped give me some ideas to try to help
supporter: It's my pleasure. I'm happy to have helped you. 
supporter: Is there anything else I can help you with? ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how are you doing today?
seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way. 
supporter: I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
seeker: Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other. 
supporter: Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.

seeker: I am feeling angry today about work. 
supporter: Oh no, what happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: My coworker expects me to do things the way she does and is constantly critical. I just want her to understand that I am able to do things my way and it is still okay. I told her this and she ignored me. 
supporter: I'm sure that's terribly frustrating having someone treat you like that. Is this something that your boss is aware of?
seeker: I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her. 
supporter: Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
seeker: That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way.

turns.content: Hey Amanda, how have you been holding up lately?
Hi, honestly, it's been a tough couple of days. I finally had the big talk with Bill, and we decided to break up.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like a really difficult decision to come to. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Yeah, it's just... we've been together for three years, but we've been stuck on what our future looks like. Our life goals just don't align anymore.
That must be so hard, especially after investing so much time and emotion into the relationship. How are you feeling about it all?
A mix of emotions, really. I feel sad and a little lost. But there's also relief, you know? Like, at least now I can move forward instead of being in limbo.
